record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Function-dependent summation for hearing the degree
record.original_question: Given an individual map f in C(S^1;S^1), or more generally in VMO(S^1;S^1), does there exist a summation process σ_{n,ε} that may depend on f and recovers the degree from Fourier magnitudes by lim_{ε→0} Σ_{n∈Z} n |an(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε} = deg f?

evidence.quote: In the same vein one can raise: Open Problem 5.7. Given any f ∈ C(S1; S1) (resp. f ∈ V MO(S1; S1)) does there exist a summation process (σn,ε) (depending on f) such that (5.25) holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1$ denote the unit circle in $\mathbb{C}$. For $f \in L^2(S^1; \mathbb{C})$, let $a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} f(e^{i\theta}) e^{-in\theta}\, d\theta$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, denote its Fourier coefficients. Recall that any $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$ (continuous maps from the circle to itself), and more generally any $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1; S^1)$ (maps of vanishing mean oscillation taking values in $S^1$), admits a well-defined integer topological degree $\deg f$.

A summation process is a family $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})_{n \in \mathbb{Z},\, \varepsilon > 0}$ of real numbers such that, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, the sum $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ is absolutely convergent.

Question: Given an individual map $f \in C(S^1; S^1)$ (respectively, $f \in \mathrm{VMO}(S^1; S^1)$), does there exist a summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$, possibly depending on $f$, such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0} \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} n\, |a_n(f)|^2\, \sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f \,?$$
artifact.category_tag: Fourier coefficients and topological degree of circle maps
artifact.status_search_result: The question (whether the degree of a VMO or continuous map of the circle can be recovered from the moduli of its Fourier coefficients via an f-dependent summation process) is part of the "Can one hear the degree?" program. While Bourgain–Kozma showed that |a_n(f)| does not determine deg f in general, the existence of an f-dependent summation process recovering the degree remains open according to available surveys on degree theory and Fourier series.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Winding numbers and Fourier series
status_evidence.snippet: Bourgain–Kozma show that |a_n(f)| do not determine deg f in general, motivating the search for f-dependent summation processes.
status_evidence.claim: Related negative result; the f-dependent version remains unresolved.
